Alex / Sofia —

Quick update from infra side after digging through the supplier records: we do have a historical stub account created in 2024 for redwood@procurely.com that never completed profile activation (status: invited -> partial_profile). That orphaned record triggers our duplicate-account guard during the invite accept flow.

Remediation steps I pushed:
- Unlinked the stale stub and cleared the email association (so a fresh invite can be accepted).
- Extended the invite token TTL by 48 hours for the new invite path to account for any timezone client-server skew.

Action for Procurely:
1) Sofia will reissue a new invite once we confirm clearance.
2) If you don't see the invite within 30 minutes, check spam and then copy/paste the acceptance URL in an incognito window.

Note: I also added a temporary acceptance logging hook (invite_accept_debug) so if you still see the error I can pull the server logs and the exact reject reason.

Attachments: screenshot of the orphaned record entry (ops-stub-2024.png) — attached to this thread.

Ben Carter
Partner Operations Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — that worked. I accepted the new invite at 2026-11-26T15:30:12-08:00 in an incognito window and completed our vendor profile. I attached the signed W-9 for your records (procurely-w9-signed.pdf).

Two quick notes for the team:
- The password reset earlier was being routed to a different mailbox due to a forwarding rule we forgot (internal on our side) — so that explained why resets never arrived.
- The acceptance URL had a trailing query param (?utm_source=mailchimp) added by our email system; when I removed it the flow completed. Not sure if Redwood's validator treats unknown query params as a mismatch — could be a brittle parser.

If helpful, I'm happy to hop on a 15-min call to walk through the steps so you can reproduce.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Alex
